# FLX-3514: a Kafka topic will not take the stream as it is

**Family:** seam/conformance (the 3000 band)

The record timestamp is the event's time, and the sink never moves a record's bytes to fit a topic. A topic whose message.timestamp.type is LogAppendTime would replace event time with the time of the write, a snapshot's topic must be compacted, and a timestamp outside the topic's message.timestamp.before.max.ms or after.max.ms, or at or below zero (the brokers refuse a negative timestamp and a producer reads 0 as the current time), is refused. An unpaced stream without commit-every is one transaction, and one that cannot finish within transaction-timeout is aborted. The message names the topic and the limit. Configure the topic for the backfill (CreateTime, compaction, wider timestamp limits), choose another topic with --sink-opt topic.EXPOSE=NAME, run a window nearer the present, or for a stream that is too long for one transaction raise transaction-timeout (and the brokers' transaction.max.timeout.ms) or pass commit-every=SECONDS to commit it as it goes.
